analysis:
Both units are base-side text of QwenTensorParallelBatchSessionTests.swift, a test-only file under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests. The change adds an optional `kind` parameter to the `Owned` test helper init (lines 58-61), which falls back to the QWEN_TP_BATCH_KV environment default. It also adds a new test, buildAheadDecodeTakesTheReadThenBuildTokensAndLogprobs (head lines 590-793), for build-ahead submitDecode/readDecode on the native TP executor. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the new test body past the first lines was not visible. The production code behind it (QwenTensorParallelNativeBatchExecutor submitDecode/readDecode) is not in the supplied evidence.

The visible test code has no production attack surface. It uses synthetic fixtures and in-process rendezvous, with no network, key, attestation or billing paths. The prefix-cache tests in the base text use temporary directories and fixed synthetic keys, not real KEKs. Relevant threats are T-041 (prefix cache scoping, TTL) and TB-007 (inference engine), but this change only adds or alters tests.

Open question for integration: whether the production build-ahead path (submitDecode/readDecode) preserves fail-closed handling of non-finite logits, per-row sampling isolation and lane retirement, as the existing selection-boundary tests check. That code is outside this batch. No finding is raised, but the unreviewed production change keeps this from being a full clearance.
